Pattern for 'gate access, then serve a private file' (e.g. a data-room share link): upload with `kind=private` so the file lands at /uploads/private/... (that raw path is 403 without a signed URL). Then a flow validates whatever it needs (share token, password, rate limit, item-belongs-to-room) and ends with `run: serve_file` to stream the bytes.

`run: serve_file` reads the file off disk directly (path clamped to the app's uploads/ dir, traversal-guarded) and streams it with Range + correct Content-Type. The flow IS the authorization - works for `auth: none` (anonymous) callers, no session and no signed URL needed, and nothing leakable escapes (unlike redirecting to a signed URL, which is a shareable bearer token for its TTL).

Example: `- run: sql … (look up item, check it belongs to the room for params.token)` then `- if: ${{ ok }}` → `- run: serve_file` with `path: ${{ steps.item.outputs.file_url }}`, `record: { table: room_items, id: '${{ steps.item.outputs.id }}' }` (names the row that owns a private file the anonymous caller did not upload; without it the uploader rule is only advisory for now, and `benmore check` warns; the row must reference the file and belong to its uploader or the uploader's tenant, see api({at:'uploads'}) → private_ownership), `disposition: ${{ params.dl == '1' && 'attachment' || 'inline' }}`. inline = View, attachment = Download; any other value serves inline. Active content (.html/.svg) is force-downloaded even when inline is requested (XSS guard).

On the hosted media CDN: a view (inline) answers 302 to the CDN URL (signed when private), whose stored headers decide how it opens, so `filename:` does not apply to it. A download (`disposition: attachment`) streams the object through the app with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<filename:, else the stored name>"` (the name follows run: proxy's rule on every backend: letters, digits, space, dot, dash and underscore only, and its extension is the stored file's, so `export.html` on a CSV is sent as `export.csv`), `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and Range support; the signed URL is made for that request and never reaches the caller. A streamed download must finish within the platform's request window (about five minutes); link to the file itself for very large media. `filename:` may be a `${{ }}` template.
